newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan president to visit Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan president to visit Mexico.

text.p: Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu is scheduled to begin a three-day visit to Mexico on Sunday to thank Mexicans for supporting Guatemala's peace process, the government said on Friday.

"The principal motive is to present in a direct and personal manner our thanks to the Mexican people, government and President Ernesto Zedillo for the very valuable support offered during the peace negotiations," Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein told reporters.

Government negotiators and leftist rebels met in Mexico City during several years of peace negotiations. The talks ended in an historic peace treaty signed in Guatemala City on Dec. 29 that put an end to 36 years of civil war.

Stein said Arzu will visit refugee camps in southern Mexico that sheltered tens of thousands of Guatemalan refugees over 15 years, mainly Mayan Indian peasants fleeing the army's brutal counterinsurgency campaigns.
The Guatemalan government is urging refugees who remain in Mexico to return home. Mexico has offered permanent residency to those who want to stay there.
Arzu and Zedillo will meet for a work session in Mexico City on Monday to review advances in economic development programmes at the Mexico-Guatemala border.

The presidents will sign an agreement to build a natural gas pipeline from Mexico to Guatemala City. Private firms in both countries are interested in financing construction of the pipeline, Stein said.
